articles.title: Nvidia will officially bring DLSS 5 to older GPUs — but won’t give gamers full control
articles.summary: Nvidia will bring DLSS 5 to RTX 40, but won’t confirm that previously announced DLSS 5 games will still ship with the tech.
articles.body: Officially, Nvidia’s controversial DLSS 5 AI rendering was supposed to launch this evening with only a single game, only on Nvidia’s latest RTX 50 GPUs, and with developers in full control of their artistic vision. But unofficially, modders have already ported a leaked version of DLSS 5 to run on just about anything while cranking sliders to the max. Now, Nvidia is changing its plans. DLSS 5 is still launching first on RTX 50 GPUs, but it’s officially coming to older RTX 40-series GPUs as well, Nvidia spokesperson Rajal Maharaj confirms to The Verge. “Our current focus is on optimizing performance for the GeForce RTX 50 Series with model updates expected later this fall. Once RTX 50 Series performance is more fully tuned, we plan to work on expanding official support to the GeForce RTX 40 Series,” reads part of Nvidia’s statement. What about earlier RTX 30 and RTX 20-series GPUs, which modders successfully targeted as well, assuming you count “not exactly playable framerate and plenty of crashes” as successful? “Right now the focus is of course on 50-series,” Maharaj tells me. “Once we feel like the 50-series is in a good place, we’re going to look at the 40-series.” Now that the cat’s out of the bag, will gamers get full control over DLSS 5’s sliders the way modders already do? Nvidia says no: “For gamers, DLSS 5 is a simple on-or-off toggle,” the company confirms. “The more granular artistic controls are for developers, including model selection, Structure Intensity, Tone Intensity, automatic masking and custom per-pixel masking.” That said, the company tells me that developers could pass along certain controls in their own settings menus, like they’ve done with other graphics tech. (Early DLSS Super Resolution was also just an on/off toggle, but today’s games let you pick between varying levels of quality or even an exact percentage, depending on the game.) Assuming you don’t mind DLSS 5, one of the benefits is that it’s easy to integrate. Developers don’t need to tell DLSS 5 which objects are “silverware” and which are “furniture” because the AI models can automatically recognize and isolate objects in a scene, distinguishing between faces, textiles, foliage, and more to apply different amounts of AI processing. Game engines that already know which video game objects are which can help DLSS 5, too: > For more targeted control, semantic AI masking can automatically recognize scene objects, while engine-level masking allows artists to isolate specific props or groups of assets, such as glassware, water droplets or foliage, and apply custom neural lighting adjustments to those elements. Unreal Engine 5 has a native plugin, and Nvidia also has SDKs. Nvidia says developers can apply DLSS 5 to their entire game this way, or do it differently for different scenes, cutscenes, or portions of gameplay, and the company tells The Verge that its DLSS 5 models run on every single frame, so there’s no minimum framerate for it to work. We’re still waiting to find out if the early backlash against DLSS 5 scared away publishers and developers that had originally committed to the technology. Nvidia’s response to us today suggests that perhaps some companies have backed away. When we asked if the company could re-confirm that it will come to Assassin’s Creed Shadows, Hogwarts Legacy, Starfield, Resident Evil Requiem, and the other 12 originally-announced titles, this was the company’s only reply: “More games are on the way. Many developers are actively integrating DLSS 5, and we’ll share updates on upcoming titles as partners finalize their integrations.”

articles.title: Original Gran Turismo Circuit Returns to Series After 13-Year Absence
articles.summary: Polyphony Digital has revealed Gran Turismo 7’s next major update will mark the return of Autumn Ring, and includes a dozen new cars, the series debut of real-life circuit Sportsland Sugo, and a variety of other features.
articles.body:
Polyphony Digital has revealed Gran Turismo 7’s next major update will mark the return of Autumn Ring , and includes a dozen new cars, the series debut of real-life circuit Sportsland Sugo, and a variety of other features.

The ‘Spec IV’ update will be delivered in two parts before the end of 2026; the first will arrive in October and the second will be available in December.

The first chunk of Spec IV will come with Sportland Sugo (a real-life race circuit located in Japan’s Miyagi Prefecture that currently hosts Super GT and Super Formula rounds) plus six new cars, a new ‘Vintage’ section featuring cars not available to purchase in GT as new, a ‘Car Concierge’ function players can use to order used and Legend cars, new driving challenges, a new car viewer, and a Collector Level cap increase.

The second half of Spec IV will include Autumn Ring, another six new cars, a new ‘Family’ mode for inexperienced players, a luck-based race with random cars called ‘Shuffle Race’, online drift trials, and a new difficulty level in the Power Pack.

Autumn Ring, first seen in the original Gran Turismo, was last included in 2013’s Gran Turismo 6. The GT7 version of Autumn Ring will include the original layout, and a new “greatly expanded layout.”

The news comes out of PlayStation’s latest State of Play showcase, which aired earlier today. Highlights from the showcase included an extended look at Square Enix’s Final Fantasy VII Revelation, a clip from Zach Cregger’s upcoming Resident Evil movie, and the reveal of two new limited-edition DualSense controllers inspired by GTA 6 , but it was a presentation that was otherwise dominated by continued fan demands for Destiny 3 .

articles.title: Amid Concern in Japan, Dragon Ball Producer Toei Animation Denies Involvement in Saudi-France Paris Theme Park
articles.summary: Last week, France and Saudi Arabia made the surprise announcement that the Paris region of France will be getting a Dragon Ball theme park. This sparked varied reactions across the internet, with many comments in Japanese expressing concern regarding licensing rights and the lack of Japanese representation. This week, Dragon Ball anime producer Toei Animation released an official announcement denying involvement in the project. So what is happening with this proposed Dragon Ball theme park in France?
articles.body:
Last week, France and Saudi Arabia made the surprise announcement that the Paris region of France will be getting a Dragon Ball theme park . This sparked varied reactions across the internet, with many comments in Japanese expressing concern regarding licensing rights and the lack of Japanese representation. This week, Dragon Ball anime producer Toei Animation released an official announcement denying involvement in the project. So what is happening with this proposed Dragon Ball theme park in France?

In case you missed it, Saudi Arabia’s de facto ruler Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman made a two-day state visit to France last month, attending the closing ceremony of the Esports World Cup in Paris alongside French president Emmanuel Macron (source: Arab News ). This trip culminated in the surprise announcement of a new theme park project just outside Paris.

Posting on X in French on August 25, Macron said: “With Saudi Arabia, we are making an unprecedented announcement.” The French president went on to describe the proposal as three theme parks located in Cergy-Pontoise, northwest of Paris. He cited the 6 billion euro investment and predicted 22,000 jobs created by the project as something that hadn’t been seen “since Disneyland Paris.” It will be a “new global destination — here, in France.”

In the post, Macron mentioned his personal liking of Japanese comics (“You know of my interest in manga”), however he did not directly state what themes these three parks would have. However, a later official press release by the Île-de-France region on August 31 referred directly to one of the three being “a Dragon Ball park.”

News outlets worldwide, including Japanese ones like Mainichi Shimbun , swiftly picked up the story of a Dragon Ball theme park in France. However, this sparked backlash among some Japanese language commenters amid concerns that there was no visible Japanese representation or official announcement from license holders at the time.

Since then, Toei Animation, the studio behind the Dragon Ball anime, issued a statement regarding the park proposal, denying any prior knowledge or involvement.

“Recently, some media reports have suggested that ‘the decision has been made to build a Dragon Ball theme park in France,’ however our company (...) and relevant rights-holding companies have not granted any licences in relation to this matter, and we are not aware of any such plans,” stated Toei Animation.

Toei Animation is involved in the ongoing plan to build a Dragon Ball theme park in the Saudi Arabian capital of Riyadh, in a strategic partnership with Qiddiya Investment Company. In this case, Toei Animation directly announced the project on its website back in 2024, alongside concept images, a video and details of the project.

Dragon Ball Z Theme Park Concept Art (2024)

However, in its recent statement, Toei clarified that the concept images used by some news reports of a Paris park actually relate to the planned Dragon Ball theme park in Riyadh, and not to any France-based project. Although new Dragon Ball projects were announced at the 40th anniversary event in April, the rights to the franchise are complicated and involve several companies. Until further official announcements are made, it’s unclear if and when a France-based theme park featuring the late Akira Toriyama’s creations will become a reality. No opening date has been set, and construction is expected to take several ​years.

Saudi Arabia’s Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman is an open fan of video games and anime, making increasing investments in game companies through his MiSK foundation and its subsidiaries. Through related companies, he owns King of Fighters developer SNK, plus a 10% stake in Capcom , among others. The Qiddiya Investment Company, which is involved in the Dragon Ball Riyadh theme park, is owned by the Saudi Arabian sovereign wealth fund, the Public Investment Fund (PIF), of which the crown prince is chairman. On August 4, an investor group composed of PIF, Silver Lake and Affinity Partners completed a $55 billion leveraged buyout of video game giant EA .

Photo by LOU BENOIST / AFP via Getty Images.

Verity Townsend is a Japan-based freelance writer who previously served as editor, contributor and translator for the game news site Automaton West. She has also written about Japanese culture and movies for various publications.

articles.title: Marvel Secretly Developing New Live-Action Disney+ Project, Potentially Young Avengers or New Mutants
articles.summary: A flurry of reports point to Marvel secretly mounting a new live-action Disney+ series, potentially featuring characters from the Young Avengers or New Mutants.
articles.body:
A flurry of reports point to Marvel secretly mounting a new live-action Disney+ series, potentially featuring characters from the Young Avengers or New Mutants.

Last month, Murphy's Multiverse spotted that a fresh Marvel production company, Veil Productions, had been set up for a TV project. Now, there's also word on its production codename: "Slumber Party."

Marvel typically sets up a production company for each of its major projects, and these can be named something referencing the project itself. (Marvel's recent "Throttle Productions" is believed to be the team behind Ryan Gosling's upcoming Ghost Rider, for example.) So too with its production codenames, though these can also be deliberately obtuse.

The Most Surprising Avengers and Marvel Characters Not Announced for Doomsday

So, what could Veil refer to? In the Marvel comics, Veil was a young member of the Avengers Academy, and Slumber Party certainly points to a youthful setting. It's also the title of New Mutants #21, which introduced Warlock.

Marvel has been considering a standalone Young Avengers project for years, it is widely understood, with teases in several other MCU projects and an array of characters it could now include. Iman Vellani's excellent Ms. Marvel was last seen trying to form a team with Hailee Steinfeld's Kate Bishop, with Kathryn Newton's Cassie Lang also in their sights to recruit.

Beyond these, it's been years now since we checked in with Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness's America Chavez and The Falcon and the Winter Soldier's Patriot. There's also Ironheart's Riri Williams, plus Agatha and Vision Quest's Maximoff twins. Even Hulk has a son now, too.

When might we hear more? Marvel will hold a dedicated "Up Next From Marvel Television and Marvel Animation" panel at New York Comic-Con on October 8, which seems like a great time to make some form of announcement. Expect more detail on Vision Quest and Daredevil: Born Again Season 3 at the same time.

Every Confirmed Mutant in the MCU (So Far)

Any new Disney+ live-action series confirmation would be notable at this point, following the noticable slowdown in new Marvel (and Star Wars) live-action series getting the greenlight. After years of pumping out projects that left fans feeling like the studio was focused on quantity rather than quality (Secret Invasion, looking at you), Disney appears to have reigned in its balance sheet, while Marvel looks to be applying more quality control.

The timing for a Young Avengers project would also seem to make sense, perhaps focusing on the characters during or directly preceding the events of Avengers: Doomsday, making for a intriguing setup to Avengers: Secret Wars.

Earlier this week, it was reported that Noah Jupe had joined the cast of Avengers: Secret Wars in a hush-hush role that fans already believed they have sussed out.

articles.title: PUBG: DED.NET Developer Argues Making a Game for the Mass Market Where 'Nobody's Too Offended and Everybody Kind of Likes It' Has Become 'Box Office Poison'
articles.summary: PUBG: DED.NET developer Dave Curd has argued that making a video game for the mass market where "nobody's too offended and everybody kind of likes it" has become "box office poison."
articles.body:
PUBG — the battle royale that popularized the genre — already has a number of spinoffs. But none is as love it or hate it as DED.NET .

Like PUBG, DED.NET is a multiplayer first-person shooter that revolves around outlasting your enemies, but there are a number of key differences. Chief among them is roguelite progression that persists across runs, and a heavy-handed 1990s aesthetic dubbed “Grunge House.” But there’s more. Matches — even if you make it to the end — will come in at around the 25-30 minute mark, which makes it a digestible experience relative to PUBG’s more intense, longer-lasting battle royale. And while PUBG is available on console, DED.NET is built from the ground up for consoles.

Set in Cascadia in 1996, a world inspired by the Pacific Northwest of the 1990s, and with a reimagining of the PUBG formula beyond battle royale, DED.NET may prove divisive. That, creative director Dave Curd told IGN at gamescom, isn’t just okay — it’s exactly what the developers at Krafton want. In fact, Curd argued that making a game for everyone has become “box office poison.”

“Definitely PUBG was the one that brought the genre to prominence and then everyone was like, ‘What's my take? Is it destruction? Is it competitive play? Is it Twitch reactions?’ And you're picturing the games as I'm describing them,” Curd began.

“And ours is the rogue. This is the rogue version where you're always chasing a build, getting into hilarious shithousery along the way. You're telling hysterical stories, you're engaging in a world filled with Twin Peaks, X-Files, David Kronenberg, body horror. We're trying to make a real evocative, love it or hate it experience.

“I think the age of making something for the mass market... which, what is that anymore? I don't think that's safe. I don't think that's smart. I think making something that can really get a fandom, something where people feel seen and they connect with, and have just as many detractors, I think that's wiser than kind of, ‘Well, let's make sure nobody's too offended and everybody kind of likes it.’ So we're trying to be sexy, evocative, gory.”

Curd said the inspiration for DED.NET ’s Grunge House aesthetic includes grunge band Nirvana, Italian zombie movies, Grindhouse, and Tarantino movies. And, he believes that if DED.NET proves “sticky,” he expects other battle royale developers to give the ‘rogue multi-match journey’ mechanic a try.

“But what they won't be able to do is replicate our world where you can chop your hands off and replace them with machetes and have a standoff in a cult mansion, underground cellar filled with bodies,” he insisted. “We're just trying to serve up something fresh for the kids.”

What Curd is desperate to avoid here is apathy. He wants DED.NET to provoke a reaction, whether that’s good or bad. If it’s good, then great. If it’s bad, well Curd can work to turn that feeling around. But apathy is a death sentence for any video game’s prospects.

“I think middle of the road is box office poison,” Curd said. “You want lovers and haters. Haters care enough to hate, which means maybe you can reach them one day. Maybe a lot of people will see this and naturally say, ‘Hey, I don't want a Ford Bronco. I want a Ford Mustang. Keep fixing the Ford Mustang.’ And that's a very valid point. And my job is not to convince you to like cheese if you're not a cheese guy. But I think there's a lot of guys that will try it and say, ‘Okay, I'm pleasantly surprised. I'm in. They're taking a swing.’

“I've always said audiences will forgive anything but being bored. I think even if they hate us, they may respect us for taking a big swing, especially when a lot of the other big players circle their wagons, they focus on one mega product. PUBG and Krafton are out here trying to serve the fans and take big swings and try new stuff.”

Curd isn't alone in making this argument. Arrowhead, the developer of smash hit co-op shooter Helldivers 2, have long argued much the same. Indeed, Arrowhead's studio tagline is, "A game for everyone is a game for no one." This, Arrowhead has said, is why mechanics like friendly fire are always enabled in Helldivers 2. Yes, it makes the game more punishing, but it also helps it stand out.

Curd said that DED.NET betas and playtests have already shown evidence of a positive response to the game, and the initial spark of a fandom revolving around its characters.

“The initial nine roster of characters have relationships with each other, with the map. They have quests outside of Win the Chicken Dinner. They have allies and rivals on the roster that you would kind of learn about,” Curd explained.

“If I ping an ally or I revive a rival, you'll kind of get that in the VO and start to understand those relationships. We're talking two or three days into our last play test, we're getting fan art depicting these love triangles. And I wasn't expecting people to get it so soon. And that shows me some people are hyper engaging with the world and becoming actual fans and not product speak audience fans. Like real people that love the world. And that's been incredibly validating for myself and the team.”

Curd, who has worked on PUBG for nine-and-a-half-years as a creative director, said that DED.NET began life as a response to a task he was set by his boss of “spreading the gospel of PUBG to the non-believers.”

“We got a lot of fans,” he said. “We got a lot of people that love our thoughtful, cerebral, tactical gameplay. See a guy 500 feet away, do you take the fight? Do you get in the car? Do you retreat? But it's not for everybody. But we think the theme of PUBG, of survival of the fittest or dog eat dog or desperate survival, it's a good juicy theme. I think you could make a PUBG Match-3! And that might be what I pitch next!

“Can we find a different audience that would still engage with that vibe and engage with that world and engage with that IP? So I think, ‘Okay, so don't make more PUBG, but find more PUBG fans. Where do you begin?'

“So it sounds kind of maybe stupidly obvious, but I just made a list. It's like, what is cool shit that PUBG does well? Number one, it's an infinite story engine. One match, survival of the fittest, one winner, 99 losers. And I think it's endured for 10 years because anyone I talk to can tell me usually in high detail about their first Chicken Dinner. So that's the first thing you think. Well, what's the opposite of that? Could that infinite story engine persist over multiple matches? And so that was the first idea that's like, that sounds good and that would not work in PUBG because it breaks that promise of perfectly fair, perfectly balanced, single shot adventure.

“Could it be a multi-match journey? What does that mean? Originally our cheesy internal lingo was body persistence. And it was, if you swim, you'll get hypothermia and you'll be coughing. And if you get shot in the head, your ears will ring for a long time. And as we stood it up and tried it, we found that it changed the way that fans would play. They were not playing to win. They were playing to not get hurt. They're like, ‘This sucks. We don't like this.’ And it's like, oh, what if the injuries were more interesting and told better stories, just sneezing in the smoke or it hurts when you swim, or you occasionally fumble your weapon on weapon swap and you swear, or maybe you have a tick where you constantly spam taunts and give away your position? Or my favorite one, Stuntman, where when you slide or dive, occasionally there's an explosion behind you because it looks cool, but it might hurt you. It might frag your teammates.

“The genesis was I love hero shooters, but I never find exactly my favorite one. I always end up settling for the one I hate least. It's never the right combination of look and abilities for what I'm after. So we thought, could we challenge the player to go on a multi-match adventure where they're picking and choosing and making interesting decisions about who they want to be when they grow up, while managing these hilarious and weird injuries and racing against a clock of a diminishing career HP of you can only play so many before you're overwhelmed by injuries and you have to retire? That's the genesis of the product.”

Players can now also register for the upcoming closed beta. There’s no release window yet, but PUBG: DED.NET is due out on PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X and S.
